item.title: Russia's war in Ukraine: the situation
item.description:
Russia carried out a drone strike on a Ukrainian railway station that killed 13 people, and attacks on aid vehicles continue in the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky where a localized cease-fire entered its third day. The independent newspaper Novaya Gazeta announced it will shut down after pressure from the Kremlin. Protests over the presence of the Russian foreign minister led to the cancellation of the G20 family photo. The conflict caused 75,767 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Israel, Gaza and the West Bank: the situation
item.description:
Israel intensified a crackdown in Hebron, displacing thousands and prompting a UN rights office warning of an ethnic cleansing nightmare, while Israeli forces demolished homes of Palestinians blamed for a Hebron shooting. Israeli drones struck the southern Gaza Strip, wounding 14 people, and IDF strikes in Gaza killed a Hamas commander who had held hostages and four Hamas operatives in separate attacks. Shin Bet is allowing Hamas operatives to choose whether they are killed alone or with their families, and settlers attacked West Bank olive harvesters, wounding at least three. The UN Commission reported war crimes and genocide even after a Gaza ceasefire, and 21,440 battle-related deaths occurred in 2024, according to UCDP.

Qatar's negotiators have returned to Tehran for a last-ditch mediation effort and Pakistan's army says it is cautiously optimistic about US-Iran mediation. JD Vance has sent a letter to Iran's president urging a restart of peace talks, and the United States cancelled the G20 family photo after European ministers refused to stand with Russia's Lavrov. 123 battle-related deaths occurred in 2024, according to UCDP.

Flash floods across Syria killed five people, including children, and injured several others. item.title: Iraq: the situation
item.description:
Iraqi security forces dismantled a drug-trafficking network, arresting 31 suspects, while Erbil police detained four suspects in a woman’s murder. Prime Minister Al-Zaidi assumed direct control of the intelligence service and is advancing talks with Damascus on the Sharaa pipeline, border security and oil exports through Baniyas, including a proposal to ship two million barrels per day. Iranian-linked attacks continued, with a Navy corpsman and Marine Raiders rescuing French soldiers from a burning building after an Iranian strike, and a memorial was unveiled in Erbil for victims of the 2024 Iranian missile attack. Chinese missiles have been reported in Iraq, adding a new external dimension. 396 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Ethiopia: the situation
item.description:
Army drones have struck displaced persons camps in South Wollo and Amhara, killing civilians including children, while armed clashes between Oromo and Somali groups in Moyale have forced thousands to flee into Kenya. Gunfire is being heard near the Ethiopian-Kenya border as civilians continue to evacuate, and Ethiopia and Eritrea have now severed diplomatic ties, raising regional tension. Russian Su-35 fighter jets and S-400 air defence systems have been deployed in Ethiopia as fighting spreads across Tigray, Amhara and Oromia. The UCDP recorded 2,824 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.

item.title: Somalia: the situation
item.description:
Al-Shabaab fighters are stepping up attacks on Turkish-trained Somali troops in Lower Shabelle and ambushing units near Baidoa, and they killed a former al-Shabaab finance chief in Lower Shabelle. African Union peacekeepers are withdrawing from four bases in Lower Shabelle, while Ethiopia is pulling more than 3,000 troops from Somalia, further reducing external military presence. The Somali federal government has agreed to acquire Pakistani JF‑17 fighter jets and the United States has imposed entry conditions on ships calling at Somali ports. The UAE carried out its first drone strike against Al-Shabaab in nearly a year and piracy off Somalia’s coast is rising, with hijacked oil tankers and hostages reported. The conflict caused 2,284 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
